observations.title: The Unanswered Command
inspection: A second rubbing lies beside the small paw and two hands. Its border is the same split loop.
Inside a ring of restraints: "Stand where we set you. Answer only when commanded. Give no bond."
The watcher faces out of the ring. The hands on this sheet pull tight; the small paw is nowhere beside them.
ownerLines: The first hands held a paw. These hands hold it down. Same border, different work. Please do not mistake one for the other.

maren: We tie shelter ropes so someone has a place to rest. A knot that takes their choice away is another thing.
wren: I copied the commands exactly. Whoever wrote them wanted an answer, but would not listen. That feels like the missing bit.

observations.title: Before the Joined Shadow
inspection: A survey sheet rests beside the painted inlet. Three entries follow one another down the edge.
First: "The shore loses its colour and its remembered shape. The measuring stones remain."
Next: "A tamer and a creature approach together. Their shadows are separate."
Last: "Two figures, one shadow. The last colour leaves this inlet." The rest of the sheet is missing.
ownerLines: Rysa kept the last witness. This is an earlier hand. The shore was already going before those two came together. Both saw truly.

maren: People remember the brightest moment. A quieter thing can have begun long before it. Keep both accounts on the table.
wren: I had the bright part underlined. Now I am drawing an arrow back. The trouble was there before the light.

observations.title: The Friend Between Them
inspection: Two surviving leaves share the ferry tally border. On the first, a tamer, a partner and the watcher share food beneath a shelter.
The watcher comes toward an open hand. No rope holds it there.
On the next leaf, the same watcher stands inside the restraint ring. A separate dark shape bends behind it.
The shore is rubbed pale as the shape spreads. The two familiar figures stand facing their friend.
Two figures, one shadow. At that mark the spreading shape stops. The next part of the leaf is torn away.
Four witness copies lie beside it. Each keeps a different stretch; laid together, their folds meet at the same shelter knot.
ownerLines: They crossed with a friend before they faced it. Four copies, four pieces of that night. None of them kept what happened after.

maren: Four tellings at one supper. They were holding different edges of the same cloth. I wish someone had kept the middle with them.
wren: They had to face someone who used to sit beside them. I do not think winning made that easy. I hope they found each other again.

reveal.title: Room for Each Other
lines: Toren waits beside the warm stones. Isolde sets the rubbing, the survey and the ferry leaves between you.
toren
I thought the watcher had failed us, or slept through the trouble. These pages show how little I knew.
isolde
The watcher was their friend. It came freely to their shelter, before anyone drew that circle.
Your partner noses your open hand. You leave it open.
toren
That older order would take no bond. They wanted the watcher, and other powerful creatures, to obey without choosing.
isolde
Their ritual gave their contempt a shape. Something that fed on memory. The world began to forget itself.
toren
Colour. The depth of a valley. A shore that the stones still measured, but nobody could remember whole.
isolde
It broke the watcher and hid behind it. The pair came to stop it, and found their friend standing against them.
toren
The joining was not the beginning of the loss. Ceryn kept the earlier entries. Rysa kept the last pallor. Both are true.
isolde
Two figures, one shadow. Their bond stopped what was eating the world. It could not undo all that was already taken.
toren
After it was freed, the watcher served no one. It slept here to heal. This warmth is its rest, not its prison.
isolde
The four family tales kept four parts of one night. Different roads, back to one older people. None of us owns the whole.
toren
The Unbound of today saw the joining and blamed the bond. Their fear of captivity is fair. Their answer leaves everyone alone.
isolde
The old order wanted servants. The present Unbound want no ties at all. Neither leaves room for friends who choose each other.
Your partner steps away to sniff the stones. Then it comes back, brushing your knee. Nobody calls it.
toren
There. Not a command. Not a creature left by itself. A friend with somewhere it wants to return.
isolde
What became of the old pair? The leaf ends. Whether any hungry pieces remain, we cannot tell from these pages.
toren
The nests Veilmote keeps warm, and what Tobin saw before: other questions. We will not fill those spaces with a good guess.
isolde
You need not become one shadow to stay beside each other. You have been teaching the world that all along.
Your partner settles beside you. For a moment you listen to two breaths, taking their own time.
The far ridge draws away. A stone at your feet has a back, a side, a hollow where rain could rest.
Warmth slips between the stones instead of lying flat across them. Your shadows turn with the ground.
The world remembers room for you both. You can stand beside each other without becoming the same.

isolde: There is room beneath the branches again. Bring your friend. We can sit without stepping on each other.
nerys: The shore has its hollows back. I can watch the water return without pretending it has forgotten every storm.
toren: The warm stones still shelter a sleeper. We know more now. That does not give us the right to wake it.
vessa: Look beneath that cloud. A valley, not a picture of one. I had missed the distance without knowing its name.
olan: The reeds have space between them again. Sit by me awhile. We will hear what comes through.
senna: The bell has somewhere for its echo to go. Leave a little silence after it. Listen.
halen: A woven thing needs the spaces too. Pull every thread tight and there is nowhere left to breathe.
rysa: My witness kept the end of that night. Your pages kept the beginning. I am glad we made room for both.
